Conclusion: E-17 does not belong to the North Warehouse batch; it comes from the same source as the substance seized in 2023.

The handover form and the corridor record showed Arda going in with four packages and coming out empty-handed; the card log showed Hakan at the inner door at 01.21. The radio and the raw list showed the fourth package was found later and with different tape; the access log and Ceren’s card exposed the deletion of the record. The command office search brought up 27-118, and the laboratory tied E-17 to the same batch as that substance. The Arda line, meanwhile, yielded nothing but debt.
You can’t open every line; weighing which record will open what is the investigation itself. The one in debt may not be the suspect, only the place suspicion goes easiest.
Fatih — North Warehouse and BDS evidence office, 11–12 December 2028

After six months of surveillance, the North Warehouse was going to come up empty. Inspector Hakan Özer brought the 420 grams he had kept off the books from the 2023 seizure 27-118 in his boot and put them behind the shelf; on the radio he said ‘check again’ and then ‘found’ the package himself. Arda left the four packages on the counter and went. Knowing the laboratory would tie the profile to 27-118, Hakan went in through the inner door while Nesrin was at the back safe and took the big package back. At 03.42 that night, at Hakan’s request, Ceren deleted the E-17 pre-entry from Nesrin’s logged-in account on the command terminal and corrected the photograph label. Arda, being in debt, was expected to be the suspect.
